questions.q: What is Inversion of Control in Spring?
o: The container creates objects and supplies their dependencies
Objects call the container to start the JVM
Controllers run before services do
Beans are created in reverse alphabetical order
questions.w: You declare what a class needs, and the container wires it. Dependency injection is the main way IoC is applied.

questions.q: What is the default scope of a Spring bean?
o: Singleton: one shared instance per container
Prototype: a new instance per injection
Request: one instance per HTTP request
Session: one instance per user
questions.w: Singleton beans must be stateless or thread-safe, because many threads use the same instance.

questions.q: A singleton bean injects a prototype bean via the constructor. How many prototype instances does the singleton see?
o: One, created when the singleton itself was built
A new one on every method call
One per thread that uses the singleton
None, because the injection fails
questions.w: Use `ObjectProvider<T>`, `@Lookup` or a scoped proxy to get a fresh prototype each time.

questions.q: Why is constructor injection preferred over field injection?
o: Dependencies are explicit and final, and the class tests easily
It is the only way in which Spring can inject any bean
Spring does not support field injection at all
It makes every bean in the container prototype scoped
questions.w: Constructor injection also reveals when a class has too many dependencies, a hint it is doing too much.

questions.q: Two beans implement `PaymentGateway`. Injecting `PaymentGateway` fails with `NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException`. How do you fix it?
o: Mark one `@Primary` or select one with `@Qualifier`
Delete one of the two interfaces
Make both beans prototype scoped
Add `@Autowired(required = false)`
questions.w: You can also inject a `List<PaymentGateway>` or a `Map<String, PaymentGateway>` to use all of them.

questions.q: Two beans depend on each other through constructors. What happens at startup?
o: Spring fails with a circular dependency error
Both beans are created without a problem
Spring creates them lazily on demand
One of the beans is silently ignored
questions.w: Circular constructor dependencies cannot be resolved. Redesign by extracting a third bean or using events. Boot 2.6+ disables circular references by default.

questions.q: What is the order of a typical bean lifecycle?
o: Instantiate, inject, `@PostConstruct`, use, `@PreDestroy`
Use, instantiate, inject, `@PreDestroy`, `@PostConstruct`
Inject, `@PreDestroy`, instantiate, use, `@PostConstruct`
Instantiate, `@PreDestroy`, use, inject, `@PostConstruct`
questions.w: `BeanPostProcessor`s run around initialisation. That is where proxies for `@Transactional` and `@Async` are created.

questions.q: What does `@Configuration` with `@Bean` methods let you do?
o: Define beans in Java, even for third-party classes you cannot annotate
Replace the Maven dependencies declared in a project
Run SQL scripts against the database at startup
Create REST endpoints automatically for every bean
questions.w: `@Component` stereotypes work for your own classes. `@Bean` is for objects that need custom construction.
